name: Shuup
title: Shuup SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Shuup: 19 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; coupons, reviews, pages, countries, states and wishlist are gaps.
lede: Solid core coverage for a smaller API: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Shuup’s REST API. Coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are the recorded gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Shuup shop

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL
env.note: Your Shuup shop’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: A JWT, sent as `Authorization: JWT <token>` — Shuup accepts neither `Token` nor `Bearer`.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_KEY
env.note: HTTP Basic username, used when no token is set; meant for server-to-server calls. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_SECRET
env.note: HTTP Basic password, with the username above.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/shuup-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SHUUP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SHUUP_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_SHUUP_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_SHUUP_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
howItWorks: Shuup’s REST API accepts HTTP Basic, session and JWT authentication. The connector sends a JWT as `Authorization: JWT <token>` — the header prefix Shuup’s JWT library expects — and falls back to HTTP Basic when it has a username and password instead.
limitations: If you set `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_SECRET` for HTTP Basic, those credentials reach every visitor: SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser.

faq.q: Can I run a Shuup shop on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Shuup shop.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Shuup?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/shuup-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How does the connector authenticate with Shuup?
faq.a: With a JWT, sent as `Authorization: JWT <token>`. Shuup does not install token authentication, so `Token` and `Bearer` headers are both refused. HTTP Basic is the fallback, meant for server-to-server calls.

api.surface: The connector calls Shuup’s Django REST Framework API under `/api/shuup/`, with the JWT views at `/api/api-token-auth/` and `/api/api-token-refresh/`, an API that its source says exists only in Shuup 1.9.x and earlier.
api.auth: A shopper signs in through `POST /api/api-token-auth/`, and the JWT that comes back in the body is sent as `Authorization: JWT <token>`, kept in `localStorage` and a cookie under `access_token`, and re-issued once through `POST /api/api-token-refresh/` when a call answers 401; HTTP Basic from the key and secret is used only when no token is set.

calls.what: `GET /api/shuup/front/shop_products/` with `shop`, `ordering`, `limit` and `offset`, `GET /api/shuup/front/shop_products/{id}/` for one product and `GET /api/shuup/front/shop_products/best_selling/` for trending
`GET /api/shuup/category/` with `identifier` and `status=1` to turn a handle into a numeric id, and `GET /api/shuup/category/{id}/`
`GET /api/shuup/front/shop_products/` with `categories`, `ordering` and paging; a free-text query returns an empty result instead of a request
`POST /api/shuup/basket/new/` (with `shop` when a store id is set), `GET /api/shuup/basket/{uuid}/`, and `POST` to `add/`, `update_quantity/`, `remove/` and `clear/` under that basket
`GET` and `PATCH /api/shuup/front/user/me/`, which carry the contact’s default billing and shipping addresses

rules: Every route ends in a slash, and the connector adds one centrally, because a missing slash triggers a Django 301 redirect that drops the POST body.
Lists page with `limit` and `offset`, not `page`, and the connector always sends `limit`, since without it Shuup returns a bare array with no `count`.

The `categories` filter takes numeric ids only and a non-numeric value causes a 500, so a category handle is first looked up through `GET /api/shuup/category/?identifier=`, and an unresolved handle gives an empty result rather than the whole catalogue.
Sorting accepts only `name`, `price` and `newest` in `ordering`, and there is no free-text search parameter, so a text search returns nothing.
Every API viewset is admin-only until a store admin raises its `api_permission_<ViewSetName>` level, so the connector names that setting in the error whenever Shuup answers 403.
